title: The Beacons and the Broken Ritual
dek: Two beacons divide the company’s judgment. Quake breaks a summoning on the coast, but the dead, a collapsing chapel and the journey still ahead complicate the victory.

facts.People: Quake; Wren; Elenia; Adelia; Dale; Saray; Alyhotep bin Baladin
facts.Outcome: The summoning fails; the company escapes the collapse, with the dead and the ritual’s full design unrecovered

body:
Rain passed through the ground in Pristinia, and Quake’s staff revealed rival lights. The company followed the northern beacon first. By the time screams turned them east, a blood ritual was drawing a figure into the world and people were already dead.

The fight would stop the summoning. It would not tell them everything they needed to know about it, or settle how they should judge the choice that had brought them there.

Rain that missed the world

Quake was going about an ordinary day when the staff on his back began to glow. Its radiance carried a trace of corruption. Across Pristinia, reality became difficult to trust: sounds felt hot, the air had a taste, and familiar sights seemed to make noises of their own. Dale struck a wrong chord. Wren and Saray sought other people who had noticed it.

Saray saw drops of rain pass through the ground. Once she pointed them out, others could see them too, but those strange drops did not wet her hand. Quake saw two beacons when he held the staff: pale light to the north and a dark, pulsing pillar to the east. Adelia saw neither until she touched the staff herself. When several people held it, the lights shifted and blended; with Quake alone holding it, the route became clear.

Quake believed the staff needed purification and wanted to strengthen the light. Elenia suggested following the light it revealed. Wren wanted to investigate the previous battle and find out what others knew. Saray worried someone might be luring them into a trap for the powerful object. They gathered food, animals and equipment, and fetched the Sword of Truth from the tavern before setting out toward the Thundering Coast.

The world’s distortion was observed. What caused it, whether the staff could be trusted, and what the beacons promised were questions the travelers carried into the journey.

The light first

Halfway toward the coast, tracks led east. Quake saw signs of several people following one; Wren recognized the make of the travelers’ footwear and counted about fifteen sets of tracks. They were only hours old and appeared hurried. Smoke was rising where the crimson pillar stood.

Adelia carried the sword and let Elenia touch it. Both could see the distant smoke. Elenia thought people might be hurt and questioned what the sword’s truth actually showed: the present, a possible future, the past, or something else. Adelia trusted an object she had used before. Elenia did not accept its name as an answer.

The company argued over the tracks. Dale wanted to help if someone was in danger. Quake recalled dying during an earlier attempt to rescue the Weary Traveler’s companions. He would continue north with the staff, he said; the others must choose. Saray went with him because she feared risking it. Wren was torn but stayed with the company. Alyhotep did not want to divide them.

By evening they reached the sea. The white light lay leagues offshore, visible only through the staff’s aid, amid what looked like two worlds merging. They would need a substantial ship to reach it. To unaided eyes, the coast was calm.

Then Wren heard screams from the east. She would not wait. Saray and Dale followed, and Quake turned too: people needed them now. Adelia saw the dark pillar growing. When the company slowed for a stealthy approach, the screams stopped.

A figure in the fire

Ahead was a terraced ritual site. Bodies lay on the rocks, blood running down their sides. Acolytes lined the working, and a terrible idol seemed to fuse a skeleton with an ancient statue. Ashen drakes, formed from burned remains and filled with necrotic energy, guarded the approach. Quake apologized for choosing the light first. Elenia answered that he could not have known.

Adelia recognized a blood ritual calling forth something between an undead being and a demon. In its crimson fire, she could make out a shadowy figure drawing life out of the acolytes. Knowing there was a summoning did not identify the being completely or reveal every purpose behind it.

The companions disagreed over how much planning they could afford. Wren wanted to strike the cultist rather than spend all their strength on the drakes. Saray proposed attacking from opposite sides. Adelia wanted them to stop talking and act. Alyhotep offered encouragement, holy water and the possibility of banishment, while acknowledging limits to what he could do.

Their preparations did not pass unnoticed. As the enemy moved to finish the ritual, the company attacked. Saray put a poisoned arrow into one of the drakes. Quake advanced, urging the others to concentrate their efforts. They were fighting defenders and a closing deadline at the same time.

The company is divided

The flying devil rose into sickly moonlight, drawing strength from the ritual as it struck. Wights stayed close to protect its caster. An orc fought from one ledge, then dropped to another, contesting the company’s climb. The construct at the center kept chanting while the defenders spent their strength on the approach.

A wall of ice cut Saray, Dale and Adelia off from the others. Adelia vanished to get closer to the caster, only for allies to collide with her unseen body. Dale apologized. Around the wall, the shadows made old lies and cruel judgments feel true. Later the assault reached deeper into their minds, forcing the memory of every hurtful thing said about them upon the living fight.

Elenia pressed forward beneath her light, badly wounded and still determined to reach the site. Dale called encouragement and healing after her. Wren tried to obtain a shot at the summoner. Alyhotep struggled to make his magic connect. Quake kept advancing despite poison.

Meanwhile the forming figure grew clearer. The narrator suggested it might be a knight summoned to destroy the shard, a possibility rather than a recovered name or complete plan. Quake could feel the staff beginning to wither against his back. Adelia quietly asked Saray to be ready to strike the idol if her own attempt worked. Time spent winning ground was still time the ritual could use.

Quake breaks the working

Quake pushed beyond his limits and hurled fire at the idol. The blast shook it; the ritual snapped. The figure taking shape inside the flames dispersed into ash. A further flash ended the working and sent smoke smelling of burned flesh out of the pit.

Stopping the summoning did not stop the battle. Elenia escaped a blow she thought should have killed her. The devil still attacked and brought Alyhotep down onto a ledge. Dale kept sending healing and praise to companions trying to stay on their feet. Elenia tried humor on the guard and had to correct the punch line while retreating, an absurd moment inside a nearly fatal fight.

Saray’s thorns finally struck the troublesome flying enemy. Then Wren fell under another attack. Dale’s healing brought her back to awareness, and she moved away from the creature to steady her aim. Alyhotep recovered enough to act again; the sequence does not supply a named resurrection. He attempted banishment and later maintained the effect holding the devil at bay. His spectral jackal struck at the orc.

Quake had called for the company to hold together, and Dale had encouraged him in turn. Saray’s last arrow felled the final enemy. The ritual was broken, and those still able to move had to get everyone out.

A victory that buries the evidence

The eldritch energy faded and the staff quieted. Then the natural chapel began collapsing into the sea. The company fled past the acolytes and the fallen companions who had died trying to stop the ritual. Something about the way the bodies lay seemed strange. There was no time left to turn that observation into an investigation.

Alyhotep offered flight; Dale doubled back to help anyone who needed it. Wren, still struggling to see clearly, made her way out. On Prima’s shore, ordinary sensations returned. Sounds were sounds again, smells were smells, and stars shone above a calm sea. The eastern smoke was gone. Across the water, the thin white beacon remained.

The lost evidence mattered. The company had prevented the figure’s arrival, but the collapsing site buried what might have explained its identity and the ritual’s full design. The narrator left them with the question of what reaching the dark pillar first might have changed. That question does not establish a saved victim in an alternate outcome or a complete account of who had organized the working.

Who carries the mistake

On the cliff, Quake said his mistake had cost lives. Saray would not let him bear that judgment alone: she had agreed to follow the light. Wren reminded him that returning to the ritual had saved others from what was coming. Adelia mourned the dead. Alyhotep tended injuries and praised a defense that had prevented further evil.

It showed the way, I interpreted it wrong.Quake

Wren wondered whether the disturbance itself had tricked them; Elenia said the light had led them astray. Quake held to the need to reach it, while accepting responsibility for his reading of the choice. They still needed a ship. They had not reached the northern source simply by ending the eastern ritual.

Elenia wanted to continue that night. Wren thought the ship could wait. Adelia proposed touching the staff and sword together to see whether they reacted; Quake left that experiment for another day. Nothing in their discussion records the proposed test being completed.

Saray offered Wren a hand, and Wren took it. The company had a victory, injuries to treat and people it could not bring home. Quake thanked the others for their help. The white light remained across the water; reaching it would require another journey.
